title: HPET (High Precision Event Timer)
summary: The HPET is a hardware timer with multiple comparators (3-32). Each comparator can generate interrupts. Registers: general capabilities (period, number of comparators, 64-bit counter), general configuration (enable, legacy replacement), main counter (64-bit, incrementing at a fixed frequency), timer N configuration (enable, periodic, level/edge, interrupt route, FSB delivery), timer N comparator (value to compare against main counter).

ext.summary: The HPET is a hardware timer with multiple comparators (3-32). Each comparator can generate interrupts. Registers: general capabilities (period, number of comparators, 64-bit counter), general configuration (enable, legacy replacement), main counter (64-bit, incrementing at a fixed frequency), timer N configuration (enable, periodic, level/edge, interrupt route, FSB delivery), timer N comparator (value to compare against main counter).

structure.meaning: Period (femtoseconds per tick), number of comparators, 64-bit counter support, legacy replacement support.
Bit 0: enable (counter running). Bit 1: legacy replacement (route timer 0/1 to IRQ0/8).
64-bit counter, increments by period each tick. Read-only (or writable for sync).

Bit 0: enable. Bit 1: periodic mode. Bit 2: level/edge trigger. Bit 3: interrupt route (IRQ number). Bit 4: FSB delivery (MSI). Bits 8-13: size (32/64-bit). Bit 14: value set (for periodic). Bit 15: force 32-bit mode.
Value to compare against main counter. On match, generates interrupt. For periodic: auto-reloads (adds period).
MSI address and data for FSB delivery (if enabled).

notes: HPET replaces the PIT (8253) and RTC (CMOS) for timing.
HPET frequency is typically 14.318 MHz (or a multiple).
HPET is used for high-resolution timers (nanosecond precision).
Modern systems use the TSC (Time Stamp Counter) + HPET for timekeeping.
HPET can generate periodic or one-shot interrupts.
